reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must not judge library text's syntax on its own: a library text that is a syntactic fragment (part of a statement, a data entry, or text valid only after REPLACING or a REPLACE statement) must be accepted when the resultant program is valid, and the program's syntax (other than the COPY and REPLACE statements themselves) must be judged only on the text produced after every COPY and REPLACE is processed, so an error appears exactly when the resultant text is invalid.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.Has(2002): at 85 any COPY in library text is refused (§1985:XII.2.4 GR12, via ConstructRegistry CopyNestedLibraryText2002); from 2002 only COPY with REPLACING over nested COPY is refused
edition.MaxTextWordLength (322 at 85) and edition.HasCompilerDirectives in the library-text word scan: lexical limits, not syntax

reader.edition-search: grep Edition.Has/HasCompilerDirectives/MaxTextWordLength/DialectBehaviors in Preprocessor/CopyProcessor.cs; none of the switches makes a syntactic judgment of library text alone (GR12's nested-COPY check is a COPY-statement check, which GR8 excepts)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for GR8 itself; the nested-COPY rule beside it differs (85 GR12 refuses any COPY in produced text)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1350 and pb5732 cover text-word scanning and REPLACING that produces a comment-entry or leaves a nested COPY; library text that is a statement or data-entry fragment, text valid only after REPLACING or REPLACE, a REPLACE match spanning the library/source boundary and the error half (resultant text invalid) are not exercised

probes.printed: IF TRUE ABC / W=7 / VIA REPLACE
probes.expected: an incomplete IF, a data entry missing its VALUE literal, MOVE ++ (valid only after REPLACING ==++== BY ==7==) and BOGUS-VERB (valid only after REPLACE) are all accepted because the resultant program is valid

probes.printed: FRAGREP.cpy(1,18): error COBOL5506 unexpected '+' / FRAGPLAIN.cpy(1,12): error COBOL5506 unexpected 'DISPLAY'
probes.expected: the same fragments without the completing replacement, or copied where the resultant text is invalid, are refused, located in the library text
REPLACE works on the resultant text, so pseudo-text matching the last library word and the next source word is replaced

citations.check: OK  §1985:XII.2.4 GR8  (2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR8
OK  §1985:XII.2.4 GR1  (2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1

reader.notes: COPY and REPLACE are processed by the preprocessor into one resultant text before the parser runs; the only checks on library text alone are lexical (text-word length) and the COPY-statement checks GR8 excepts. Diagnostics on the resultant text keep the library file and line, which is correct attribution.

refuter.evidence: q6a.cob (runs/q6a-002): library text that is a data entry cut after PIC, completed by the source line after the COPY; an empty library text; a comment-only library text; and a library text that IS a 1985 REPLACE statement (§1985:XII.3.4 GR4: REPLACE is processed after COPY), whose replacement then makes the source verb XSHOW a DISPLAY; REPLACE OFF after it. Compiled and ran: 'AFTER LIBRARY REPLACE WPX' / 'END'. q6b.cob (runs/q6b-002): one DISPLAY statement split across two COPY statements (verb in HALF1, operands in HALF2), and a COPY inside an IF: 'TWO HALVESZZ9' / 'TWO HALVESQQQ' / 'IN IF'. The two refusals met while writing the probes were resultant-text errors of my own (END-IF after a period; a text-name reused as a data-name, refused under the 1985 disjoint-sets rule, a COPY-statement check GR8 excepts). Citations: OK §1985:XII.2.4 GR8 (the text is in GR8); OK §1985:XII.3.4 GR4 (the text is in GR4).
